key_insight: The paper proposes training a lightweight robotic memory module using expensive vision-language model (VLM) supervision only during training, so the robot can remember task-relevant past events without needing heavy online VLM queries at inference time.
problem_solved: Robots often need long-term memory for manipulation tasks, but conditioning on full histories is noisy, costly, and can hurt performance due to spurious correlations. This work addresses the challenge of retaining only salient, useful information efficiently.
method: Use VLM queries during training to identify which past observations and actions are task-salient.
Learn a compact workspace memory representation from this saliency-driven supervision.
At test time, rely on the lightweight learned memory instead of expensive in-the-loop VLM processing.
impact: This makes long-horizon robotic policies more practical by reducing runtime compute while preserving useful memory. For practitioners, it offers a scalable way to add memory to manipulation systems without paying the cost of heavy multimodal inference during deployment.

paper_title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
paper_authors: Nitish Dashora, Douglas Chen, Idan Shenfeld, John Marangola, Pulkit Agrawal
